Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 1) A motorboat, whose speed is 15 km/hr in still water goes 30 km downstream and comes back in a total of 4 hours 30 minutes. The speed of the stream (in km/hr) is:
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Let the speed of the stream be x km/hr. Then,
Speed downstream = (15 + x) km/hr,
Speed upstream = (15 - x) km/hr

30/(15 + x) +30/(15 - x) = 4(1/2)
900/(225 - X2) = 9/2
9X2 = 225
X2 = 25
X = 5 km/hr

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 2) A train has a length of 150 metres. It is passing a man who is moving at 2 km/hr in the same direction of the train, in 3 seconds. Find out the speed of the train?
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Length of the train = 150 m
Speed of the man = 2 km/hr
Relative speed = 150/3 = 50 m/s
= 50 × 18/5
= 180 km/hr
Relative speed = Speed of train - Speed of the man (as both are moving in the same direction).
Therefore,
Speed of the train = Relative speed + Speed of the man
= 180 + 2
= 182 km/hr

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 3) Speed of a boat in standing water is 9 kmph and the speed of the stream is 1.5 kmph. A man rows to a place at a distance of 105 km and comes back to the starting point. The total time taken by him is:
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Speed upstream = 7.5 kmph.
Speed downstream = 10.5 kmph.
Total time taken = (105/7.5 + 105/10.5) hours = 24 hours

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 4) A train 360 metre long runs with a speed of 45 km/hr. What time will it take to pass a platform 140 metre long?
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Speed = 45 km/hr = 45 × 5/18
= 25/2 m/s
Distance travelled = Length of the train + Length of the platform
= 360 + 140
= 500 metre.
Time taken to cross the platform = 500/(25/2)
= 40 seconds

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 5) A man can row three-quarters of a kilometre against the stream in 11(1/4) minutes and down the stream in 7(1/2) minutes. The speed (in km/hr) of the man in still water is -
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
We can write three-quarters of a kilometre as 750 metres, 11(1/4) minutes as 675 seconds and 7(1/2) minutes as 450 seconds.

Rate upstream = (750/675) m/sec = 10/9 m/sec
Rate downstream = (750/450) m/sec = 5/3 m/sec
Rate in still water = (1/2) (10/9 + 5/3) m/sec
= 25/18 m/sec
= (25/18 × 18/5) km/hr
= 5km/hr

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 6) A train having a length of 240 metre passes a post in 24 seconds. How long will it take to pass a platform having a length of 650 metre?
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Speed of the train = 240/24 = 10 m/s
Required time = (240 + 650)/10 = 89 seconds

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 7) A man rows to a place 48 km distant and comes back in 14 hours. He finds that he can row 4 km with the stream in the same time as 3 km against the stream. The rate of the stream is:
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Suppose he moves 4 km downstream in x hours.
Then,
Speed downstream = (4/x) km/hr
Speed upstream = (3/x) km//hr

So, 48/(4/x) + 48/(3/x) = 14
or, 12x + 16x = 14
or, 6x + 8x = 7
or, x = 1/2
So, Speed downstream = 8 km/hr
Speed upstream = 6km/hr

Rate of the stream = (1/2) (8-6) km/hr = 1km/hr

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 8) Two trains, each 500 metre long, are running in opposite directions on parallel tracks. If their speeds are 45 km/hr and 30 km/hr respectively, the time taken by the slower train to pass the driver of the faster one is -
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Relative speed = ( 45 + 30 )
= 75 km/hr
= (75 × 5)/18 m/s
= 125/6 m/s

We are calculating the time taken by the slower train to pass the driver of the faster one.

Hence, distance = length of the slower train = 500 metre
Time = 500/( 125/6)
= 24 seconds

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 9) A boatman goes 2 km against the current of the stream in 2 hour and goes 1km along the current in 20 minutes. How long will it take to go 5 km in stationary water?
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Speed upstream = 2/2 = 1 km/hr
Speed downstream = 1/(20/60) = 3 km/hr
Speed in still water = (1/2)(3+1) = 2 km/hr
Time taken to travel 5 km in still water = 5/2
= 2(1/2)
= 2 hr 30 min

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 10) A train is running at a speed of 40 km/hr and it crosses a post in 18 seconds. What is the length of the train?
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Speed = 40 km/hr = (40 × 5/18) m/s = 100/9 m/s
Time = 18 seconds
Distance Covered = 100/9 × 18 = 200 m
Therefore,
Length of the train = 200 m

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 11) The speed of a boat in still water is 22km/hr and the rate of current is 4km/hr. The distance travelled downstream in 24 minutes is:
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Speed downstream = 22 + 4 = 26 kmph
Time = 24 minutes = 24/60 hour = 2/5 hour
Distance travelled = 2/5 × 26 = 10.4 km

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 12) Two trains running in opposite directions cross a man standing on the platform in 27 seconds and 17 seconds respectively. If they cross each other in 23 seconds, what is the ratio of their speeds?
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Let the speed of the trains be x m/s and y m/s respectively.
Length of first train = 27x
Length of second train = 17y
Relative speed = x + y
Time taken to cross each other = 23s
Total distance covered while crossing each other = 27x + 17y
Therefore,
23 (x + y) = 27x + 17y
⇒ 4x = 6y
⇒ x /y = 6/4
= 3/2

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 13) A boat covers a certain distance downstream in 1 hour, while it comes back in 1 (1/ 2) hours. If the speed of the stream is 3 kmph, what is the speed of the boat in still water?
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Let speed of the water in still water = x kmph
Given that speed of the stream = 3 kmph

Speed downstream = (x + 3) kmph
Speed upstream = (x - 3) kmph

He travels a certain distance downstream in 1 hour and comes back in 1 (1/ 2) hour. That is, (distance travelled downstream in 1 hour = distance travelled upstream in 1 (1 /2) hour).

Since, distance = speed × time ; we have,
(x + 3) × 1 = (x − 3) × (3/2)
⇒ 2 (x + 3) = 3 (x − 3)
⇒ 2x + 6 = 3x − 9
⇒ x = 6 + 9 = 15

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 14) Two trains are running in opposite directions at the same speed. The length of each train is 120 metre. If they cross each other in 12 seconds, the speed of each train (in km/hr) is
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Distance covered = (120 + 120) = 240 metre
Time = 12 seconds
Relative speed = 240/ 12
= 20 m/s
= 20 × 18 /5 km/hr
= 72 km/hr
Relative speed in this case is the sum of the speeds of the trains and each train has same speed,
speed of each train = 72 /2
= 36 km/hr

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 15) A boat takes 90 minutes less to travel 36 miles downstream than to travel the same distance upstream. If the speed of the boat in still water is 10 mph, the speed of the stream is:
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Speed of the boat in still water = 10 mph
Let speed of the stream be x mph

Then, speed downstream = (10 + x) mph
speed upstream = (10 − x) mph

Time taken to travel 36 miles upstream - Time taken to travel 36 miles downstream = 90/60 hour
= 3/2 hour

⇒ 36/(10 − x) − 36(10 + x) = 3/2
⇒ 12/(10 − x) − 12(10 + x) = 1 /2
⇒ 24 (10 + x) − 24 (10 − x) = (10 + x) (10 − x)
⇒ 240 + 24 x − 240 + 24 x
= (100 − x2)
⇒ 48 x = 100 − x2
⇒ x2 + 48x − 100 = 0
⇒ (x + 50) (x − 2) = 0
⇒ x = 2 (ignoring -ve value)

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 16) Two trains of equal length are running on parallel lines in the same direction at 46 km/hr and 36 km/hr. If the faster train passes the slower train in 36 seconds,what is the length of each train?
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Let length of each train = x metre
Total distance covered while passing the slower train = (x + x) = 2x metre
Relative speed = (46 − 36)
= 10 km/hr
= 10 × 5/18
= 50/18 m/s

Time = 36 seconds
⇒ 2 x/36 = 50/18
⇒ x = 50

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 17) In a river flowing at 2 km/hr, a boat travels 32 km upstream and then returns downstream to the starting point. If its speed in still water is 6 km/hr, find the total journey time.
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Speed of the boat in still water = 6 km/hr
Speed of the stream = 2 km/hr
Speed downstream = (6 + 2) = 8 km/hr
Speed upstream = (6 − 2) = 4 km/hr
Total journey time = 32/8 + 32/4 = 12 hr

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 18) A man takes twice as long to row a distance against the stream as to row the same distance in favour of the stream. The ratio of the speed of the boat (in still water) and the stream is:
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Let speed upstream = x
Then,
Speed downstream = 2 x
Speed in still water = (2 x + x) /2 = 3x/2
Speed of the stream = (2 x − x)/2 = x/2
Speed in still water : Speed of the stream
= 3x/2 : x/2
= 3 : 1

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 19) A boat travelled upstream and then returned, stopping 4 km short of the place from which it started. Speed of the stream is 2 km/hr. If total time taken by the boat is 6 hour and its speed in still water is 4 km/hr, distance travelled upstream is :
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Let distance travelled upstream be x km
x/(4 − 2) +( x − 4)/( 4 + 2) = 6
⇒ x/2 + (x − 4)/6 = 6
⇒ 3 x + x − 4 = 36
⇒ 4 x = 40
⇒ x = 10

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 20) A boatman can row 96 km downstream in 8 hour. If the speed of the current is 4 km/hr, then find the time required to cover 8 km upstream?
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Speed downstream = 96/8 = 12 km/hr
Speed of current = 4 km/hr
Speed of the boatman in still water = 12 − 4 = 8 km/hr
Speed upstream = 8 − 4 = 4 km/hr
Time taken to cover 8 km upstream = 8/4 = 2 hrs

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 21) The speed of a boat in still water is 10 km/hr. If it can travel 78 km downstream and 42 km upstream in the same time, the speed of the stream is
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Let the speed of the stream be y km/hr.
Then Speed upstream = (10 − y) km/hr
Speed downstream = ( 10 + y) km/hr
Time taken to travel 78 km downstream = Time taken to travel 42 km upstream
⇒ 78/(10 + y) = 42/(10 − y)
⇒ 13/(10 + y) = 7/(10 − y)
⇒ 130 − 13y = 70 + 7y
⇒ 20y = 60
⇒ y = 3

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 22) A boatman can row 3 km against the stream in 20 minutes and return in 18 minutes. Find the rate of current?
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Speed upstream = 3/(20/60) = 9 km/hr
Speed downstream = 3/(18/60) = 10 km/hr
Rate of current = (10 − 9)/2 = 1/2 km/hr

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 23) A train overtakes two persons who are walking in the same direction to that of the train at 2 kmph and 4 kmph and passes them completely in 9 and 10 seconds respectively. What is the length of the train?
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Let length and speed of the train be x metre and v kmph respectively.
x/9 = (v − 2) × 5/18 ⋯ ( 1 )
x/10 = (v − 4) × 5/18 ⋯ ( 2 )
Dividing (1) by (2) gives,
10/9 = (v − 2)/(v − 4)
⇒ 10v − 40 = 9v − 18
⇒ v = 22
Substituting the value of v in (1)
x/9 = 100/18
⇒ x = 50

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 24) A boat takes 38 hours for travelling downstream from point A to point B and coming back to point C midway between A and B. If the velocity of the stream is 4 kmph and the speed of the boat in still water is 14 kmph, what is the distance between A and B?
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Velocity of the stream = 4 kmph
Speed of the boat in still water = 14 kmph
Speed downstream = ( 14 + 4 ) = 18 kmph
Speed upstream = ( 14 − 4 ) = 10 kmph
Let the distance between A and B be x km

Time taken to travel downstream from A to B + Time taken to travel upstream from B to C (mid of A and B) = 38 hour

⇒ x/18 + (x/2)/10 = 38
⇒ x/18 + x/20 = 38
⇒ 19x/180 = 38
⇒ x/180 = 2
⇒ x = 360
i.e., distance between A and B = 360 km

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 25) The speed of a boat in still water is 25 kmph. If it can travel 10 km upstream in 1 hr, what time would it take to travel the same distance downstream?
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Speed of boat in still water = 25 km/hr
Speed upstream = 10 km/hr
Speed of the stream = (25 − 10) = 15 km/hr
Speed downstream = (25 + 15) = 40 km/hr

Time taken to travel 10 km downstream = 10/40 hour
= (10 × 60)/40
= 15 minute

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 26) A man can row 7.5 kmph in still water and he finds that it takes him twice as long to row up than to row down the river. Find the rate of stream -
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Let rate of stream be y km/hr, distance be d km
time upstream = 2 (time downstream)
⇒ d/(7.5 − y) = 2d/(7.5 + y)
⇒ 2( 7.5 − y ) = 7.5 + y
⇒ 15 − 2 y = 7.5 + y
⇒ 3 y = 7.5
⇒ y = 2.5

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 27) Two trains having equal lengths take 10 seconds and 15 seconds respectively to cross a post. If the length of each train is 120 metres, in what time (in seconds) will they cross each other when travelling in opposite directions?
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Speed of first train = 120 /10 = 12 m/s
Speed of second train = 120/15 = 8 m/s
If they travel in opposite direction, relative speed = 12 + 8 = 20 m/s
Distance covered = 120 + 120 = 240 metres
Time = 240/20 = 12 seconds

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 28) A train overtakes two persons walking along a railway track. The first person walks at 4.5 km/hr and the other walks at 5.4 km/hr. The train needs 8.4 and 8.5 seconds respectively to overtake them. What is the speed of the train if both the persons are walking in the same direction as the train?
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Let length and speed of the train be x metre and y kmph
x/8.4 = (y − 4.5) × 5/18 ⋯ (1)
x/8.5 = (y − 5.4) × 5/18 ⋯ (2)
Dividing (1) by (2) gives,
8.5/8.4 = (y − 4.5)/(y − 5.4)
⇒ 8.4y − 8.4 × 4.5 = 8.5y − 8.5 × 5.4
⇒ 0.1y = 8.5 × 5.4 − 8.4 × 4.5
⇒ 0.1y = 45.9 − 37.8 = 8.1
⇒ y = 81

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 29) Two stations P and Q are 110 km apart on a straight track. One train starts from P at 7 a.m. and travels towards Q at 20 kmph. Another train starts from Q at 8 a.m. and travels towards P at a speed of 25 kmph. At what time will they meet?
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Assume both trains meet x hours after 7 a.m.
Distance covered by train starting from P in x hours = 20 x km
Distance covered by train starting from Q in (x − 1) hours = 25 (x − 1) km
Total distance = 110 km
⇒ 20 x + 25 (x − 1) = 110
⇒ 45 x = 135
⇒ x = 3
Hence, they meet 3 hours after 7 a.m.
i.e., they meet at 10 a.m.

Alternative method:
Distance travelled by first train in 1 hour = 20 km
Therefore, at 8 a.m., both trains will be (110 − 20) = 90 km apart.
Since the relative speed is (20 + 25) = 45 kmph,
they will cover this distance in 90/ 45 = 2 hours.
I.e. They will meet at 10 a.m.

Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.question: 30) A train, 800 metre long is running with a speed of 78 km/hr. It crosses a tunnel in 1 minute. What is the length of the tunnel (in metres)?
Problems on Boats & Streams, Trains.exp:
Let length of the tunnel = x metre
Then, distance = (800 + x) metre
Time = 1 minute = 60 seconds
Speed = 78 km/hr
= 78 × 5 /18 m/s
= 65/3 m/s

800 + x = 60 × 65/3
⇒ 800 + x = 1300
⇒ x = 500
